# linux_user (Resource)

Manages a user account with `useradd`, `usermod` and `userdel` (on Alpine, install the `shadow` package). An existing account is adopted. Destroying the resource deletes the account only if this resource created it.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "linux_group" "app" {
  name = "app"
}

resource "linux_user" "app" {
  name    = "app"
  comment = "Application account"
  shell   = "/usr/sbin/nologin"
  home    = "/srv/app"
  system  = true
  groups  = [linux_group.app.name, "adm"]
}

resource "linux_user" "alice" {
  name          = "alice"
  shell         = "/bin/bash"
  groups        = ["sudo"]
  password_hash = var.alice_password_hash # openssl passwd -6
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `name` (String) Name of the user.

### Optional

- `comment` (String) Comment (GECOS field), usually the full name.
- `create_home` (Boolean) Create the home directory. Only used on creation. Defaults to `true`.
- `group` (String) Primary group, which must exist. Defaults to the system default, usually a group named after the user.
- `groups` (Set of String) Supplementary groups, which must exist. When set, the user belongs to these groups only. Leave unset to not manage them.
- `home` (String) Home directory. Changing it does not move the existing one.
- `password_hash` (String, Sensitive) Password, hashed for `/etc/shadow`, such as the output of `openssl passwd -6`. It is sent on standard input. Changes made outside of Terraform are not detected.
- `remove_home` (Boolean) Delete the home directory and mail spool with the account. Defaults to `false`.
- `shell` (String) Login shell.
- `system` (Boolean) Create a system account. Only used on creation. Defaults to `false`.
- `uid` (Number) User ID. Defaults to the next free one.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Name of the user.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The ID is the name of the user.
terraform import linux_user.alice alice
```
